name: Comorian Langouste à la Vanille
description: Langouste à la vanille, lobster in a real vanilla-butter sauce, is Comoros's national dish, real technique built on genuine Comorian vanilla (one of the country's most prized exports) alongside butter, shallots, and white wine - shrimp stands in here for real lobster, a fair approximation of the technique though missing lobster's real richness.

ingredients_full.note: finely minced, standing in for shallot

ingredients.note: finely minced, standing in for shallot

steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the butter over medium heat, 3-4 minutes, until softened.
Add the wine and let it bubble and reduce for 1-2 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook 3-4 minutes until just pink.
Stir in the vanilla and vinegar off the heat, right before serving - real technique keeps the vanilla's aroma bright rather than cooking it down.

name: Comorian Pilao
description: Pilao, an aromatic spiced rice dish, is a genuine Comorian staple, real technique built on a considerably fuller spice blend than a simple garam masala rice - real versions include ginger, garlic, black pepper, nutmeg, and cloves alongside cinnamon, cardamom, and saffron, plus a real bouillon cube for savory depth, all of which were missing here before.
steps_detailed: Soak the saffron in a tablespoon of warm water for 10 minutes.
Brown the beef with the onion, garlic, and ginger, 8-9 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add the garam masala, cinnamon, cardamom, nutmeg, cloves, and black pepper, and cook 1-2 minutes until fragrant - real pilao depends on this fuller spice blend, not just garam masala alone.
Add the rice, saffron with its soaking water, bouillon, and 1.25 cups water, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.

name: Comorian M'tsolola
description: M'tsolola, a real Comorian specialty genuinely combining both beef and fish together in the same pot, slow-simmered in coconut milk with onions and tomatoes - this real dual-protein combination is distinctly Comorian.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 6-7 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and tomatoes, and simmer 20-22 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the fish and simmer 8-10 minutes more until just cooked through.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion, 6-7 minutes.

Add the fish and simmer 8-10 minutes more until just cooked through.

name: Comorian Ambrevades au Curry
description: Ambrevades au curry, a real pigeon pea curry, is a beloved Comorian vegetarian dish, real technique building depth from cumin, cardamom, and turmeric together with coconut milk.
steps_detailed: Cook the cumin, cardamom, and turmeric in a little oil, 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and tomatoes, and simmer 8-10 minutes.
Add the pigeon peas and simmer 10-12 minutes until well combined.

name: Comorian Mkatra Foutra
description: Mkatra foutra, a yeasted coconut bread, is a genuine Comorian staple - real coconut milk stands in for dairy, reflecting the islands' real lack of a dairy industry.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, coconut milk, sugar, baking powder, and egg with a little water into a thick batter.
Cook in a lightly oiled pan, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.

name: Comorian Achard aux Legumes
description: Achard aux legumes, a real pickled vegetable relish made with lemon or green mango, is a beloved Comorian side dish.
steps_detailed: Toss the cucumber and carrot with the lemon juice and turmeric.
Let sit at least 30 minutes to lightly pickle before serving.

name: Comorian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Comoros's rich Indian Ocean fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Comorian Mshakiki
description: Mshakiki, marinated and grilled beef skewers, is a beloved Comorian street food, real technique letting the meat marinate before the char of the grill.
steps_detailed: Marinate the beef in the garlic and lemon juice 15-20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill, turning, 8-10 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: Comorian Fried Plantain
description: Fried ripe plantain, a common Comorian side dish, real versions using genuinely ripe plantain for real caramelization.
steps_detailed: Fry the plantain slices in a little oil, turning once, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply caramelized and golden.
